source_refs.note: Topic 16.5 (PDF 68-71); Figs 16.6-16.7 are redrawn. The book's 'reduces the charge on the plates' is given as reducing the field, since the plate charge is unchanged. The check question is added; answer needs review.

blocks.text: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two conductors placed close together and separated by vacuum, air or another insulator called a dielectric. When the plates are connected to a battery of voltage V (Fig 16.6), the battery puts a charge +Q on the plate joined to its positive terminal and -Q on the other plate, setting up a potential difference V between them. It is found that Q is proportional to V, so Q = CV, or C = Q/V (16.28). The constant C is the capacitance of the capacitor; it depends on the geometry of the plates and the medium between them, and measures the capacitor's ability to store charge.

blocks.title: Capacitance; the farad
blocks.text: The capacitance of a capacitor is the charge on one plate needed to raise its potential by one volt with respect to the other. Its SI unit is the coulomb per volt, called the farad (F) after Michael Faraday: a capacitor has a capacitance of one farad if one coulomb given to one plate produces a potential difference of one volt between the plates.

Consider two parallel metal plates, each of area A, a small distance d apart, so that the field E between them is uniform and confined almost entirely to the region between the plates, with air or vacuum between them. Then Cvac = Q/V (16.29) and E = V/d (16.30). By Gauss's law the field between the plates is E = sigma/eo, where sigma = Q/A is the surface charge density, so E = Q/(A eo) (16.31). Equating, V/d = Q/(A eo), which gives Cvac = Q/V = A eo / d (16.32).

blocks.alt: Two parallel plates drawn at a slant, the left one yellow and marked +Q, the right one blue and marked -Q, a distance d apart, each of area A. Wires join them through a switch S to a battery of voltage V. Notes: Q is proportional to V, Q = CV, C = Q/V; SI unit the farad = C/V; Cvac = A eo / d and Cmed = A eo er / d.
blocks.caption: A parallel-plate capacitor (original diagram after Fig 16.6).
blocks.long_description: Bigger plates hold more charge at the same voltage, and closer plates make a stronger field for the same charge, so C = A eo / d grows with A and falls with d.

blocks.text: If an insulating material (a dielectric) of relative permittivity er is placed between the plates, the capacitance increases by the factor er; er is also called the dielectric constant. To see this, connect a charged capacitor to a voltmeter (Fig 16.7 a): the deflection measures the potential difference. When a dielectric is inserted, the reading falls (Fig 16.7 b). Since C = Q/V and Q stays the same while V falls, C increases: Cmed = A eo er / d (16.33). Dividing by equation 16.32 gives er = Cmed / Cvac (16.34).

blocks.title: Dielectric constant
blocks.text: The dielectric constant is the ratio of the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor with an insulating substance between the plates to its capacitance with vacuum (or air) between them.

The potential difference falls because the atoms of the dielectric are polarised. A dielectric is an insulator: it has no free electrons, and all its electrons are bound to their nuclei. In an electric field the electrons of each atom are displaced slightly, opposite to the field (Fig 16.7 c); the atom is said to be polarised. In a slab between oppositely charged plates, all the atoms are polarised (Fig 16.7 d), and charges appear on the surfaces of the slab touching the plates, opposite in sign to the charge on the adjacent plate. These partly cancel the effect of the plate charges, so the field and the potential difference between the plates decrease.

blocks.alt: Left: (a) a charged capacitor with air between its plates connected to a voltmeter reading Vo; (b) the same capacitor with a green dielectric slab between the plates; the voltmeter now reads a smaller V. Right: an atom with no field, nucleus at the centre of its electron cloud; in a field to the right the electron cloud shifts left; below, a slab between a positive and a negative plate filled with polarised atoms, each with its negative side towards the positive plate.
blocks.caption: A dielectric between the plates (original diagram after Fig 16.7).
blocks.long_description: The charge on the plates does not change when the slab is inserted, but the polarised slab weakens the field inside, so the voltage falls and C = Q/V rises by the factor er.

blocks.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.02 m^2 a distance 1.0 mm apart in air. Find its capacitance, and its capacitance with a dielectric of er = 5.

items: Q = CV; C depends on plate area, separation and medium.
Cvac = A eo / d; Cmed = A eo er / d; er = Cmed/Cvac.
A dielectric is polarised and weakens the field, so V falls and C rises.
